The recent thread on /ptg/ users being banned upset me because as a bittorrent enthusiast all parties involved from staff to users ultimately lost out and came out looking in a poor light. This isn't how conduct should be made between grown-ups and I feel like the communities which I belong to continue to have their reputations sullied each time one of these events happens.

The thread in question: https://www.reddit.com/r/trackers/comments/4fpzxd/can_you_be_banned_from_private_trackers_for/

I want to start by looking at staff actions.

yur1 of AHD: http://imgur.com/a/M9ABe

312c of PTP: https://ghostbin.com/paste/v4a8v/raw

Immediately yur1 uses a cuss in their handling of a user. This by better tracker's communication standards is unacceptable. He continues to keep cussing and his approach is wildly speculative considering it is later revealed that Bazey has their profile screenshotted and posted around. yur1 proceeds to end the conversation very aggressively and his communication and attitude is unprofessional and shows that AHD is not all too concerned with their image. This is good example of how not to communicate with your users but considering AHD's userbase size, site development progress over the years, retention of content and inability to come close to out-competing HDBits I can conclude the management is full of yur1s.

312c is generally accepted as being another poor and unprofessional communicator so I won't focus too much on their language. However 312c tries their absolute hardest to look for a reason to keep Tomoko banned. Okay so maybe Tomoko didn't infringe in any way when asking for an invite from two different staff members because they informed the slower staff member in a timely manner to disregard their previous r3quest. This is something I've done countless times and so have thousands of others. It's a non-issue. However by mere association with 4chan, which as a place of entertainment like SomethingAwful and Newgrounds is a place where many of us grew up on, 312c trumps up the charges without any actual rules being broken and decides for Tomoko to stay out of PTP.

The thing you have to understand is that there are many, many useful trackers which are very highly regarded and deserve to have you in them but are unfortunately presided over by overworked, naturally unprofessional and subjective management. At all turns of disablement you, the user, need to treat the re-enabling process like a game of chess. Can you really afford not to use every ounce of wit and brainpower to remain in a repository of the world's largest collections?

Act professional, act exactly professional like you would in a job interview or with a client or with a professor you look up to. Don't waste time lying to yourself; honesty, like What.CD and BTN always say, is the best policy. Own up to every bad thing you have done and spill the beans. Explain yourself fully and admit you were wrong. It is easier to gain sympathy when you come in with a weak position than a very strong one and where you have the moderator convince you why you should be re-enabled. If you have been disabled for a totally unrelated reason it will be obvious that you genuinely do not know the issue at hand and the moderator may have self-doubt about their interpretation of the circumstances.

Again you must always aim to out act the professionalism of the person you're dealing with. Talk formally, present your facts and knowledge of the situation clearly, do not lie, admit wrong-doing where there is wrong-doing, highlight the areas you excel in and what potential and accomplishments you have, create a picture where you have a positive future within that tracker and say plainly that you will think next time before doing whatever it is you did.

If your situation is so abysmal then accept your loss and move onto another community and begin the process of improving that one.

How not to be banned

There is a difference between being disabled and being banned. Being banned comes with your own understanding that you have broken way too many golden rules at once to even attempt approaching a disabled channel. Disablement can usually be argued but whether you face the risk of being banned or disabled, always consider that you're risking losing access to the one of the world's largest repositories of free entertainment. Always be skeptical before committing any kind of action and consider alternatives to what you're about to do which may put your account out for scrutiny.

I'm neutral on the /ptg/ matter because I can tell what happened from logs, screenshots and hearsay without being there. Not all but some users tried to find ways to invite and trade people they barely have any knowledge of. My words should stop there because first and foremost this is a fundamental security risk. It also represents allowing possibly previously banned members from re-entering which with all the monitoring methods inter-tracker staff have at their disposal is unlikely to be sustainable and only leads to them wasting staff time in the disabled channel. Years of this creates a bad and burnt out staff member and proceeds to ruin our enjoyment of that tracker.

/ptg/ users fell for some of the oldest tricks in the book. Yes, staff can post links to infrequently visited pages on their own site and later tie page visits to IP addresses and user accounts. Stop clicking on links leading back to trackers you're a member of.

Reddit is a good place for tracker discussions because tracker staff cannot do something which is possible when using a forum with [img] BBcode. They can send you a very tiny image hosted by them and when the message is viewed by you, you are inadvertently telling them your IP address when you load this invisible pixel/image in the background. Be careful of image hoster links you are note aware of.

The biggest trick in the book is they don't need one at all. Not every tracker is objective like What.CD and BTN, they don't need a good reason to keep you around. You need you around. Don't associate with any possible place of discussion which can be interpreted incorrectly. Don't try to make friends especially at places like /ptg/ because if you were try to rationalise the kind of good that can come from such a place you will find it difficult. Really it's just a place for gossip. It does not serve to better torrent retention or enlighten tracker communities. You're more likely to catch word of new ways to 'game the system', you might be enticed to cheat or to get into the spirit of giving away your invites by smooth talkers.

Ultimately please consider the impact on your life, ability to be entertaining and knowledgeable about music, movies, etc. and personal time when you put yourself in danger of breaking the rules. If you do not agree with the ideals of those rules then step away and stop using the tracker. Don't be a hero, one site may not mind what you do but they all talk to each other and you may be banned on some completely unrelated tracker just because one bad staff member like yur1 or 312c are burnt out and have lost all humility.
